title: CESTAT Kolkata: CENVAT Credit on Tippers Survives Purchase Before the Capital-Goods Notification
case_name: Libra Business Private Limited v. Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise
card_summary: Revenue denied Libra Business Rs 1.04 crore in CENVAT credit on 25 Volvo tippers bought in February-March 2010, since tippers entered the capital goods definition only from 22 June 2010. The bench of Ashok Jindal and K. Anpazhakan held eligibility turns on when the vehicles were registered and used, not purchased. As the tippers were used only after that date, the credit and the dropped penalty stood.
card_tip: Where capital-goods eligibility turns on a notification's effective date, argue from the date of registration or actual use rather than the purchase date, if that reading favours the taxpayer.
verification_notes: The Rs 1.04 crore credit figure, the 25 Volvo tippers bought February-March 2010, the 22 June 2010 notification cut-off, the bench composition (Ashok Jindal and K. Anpazhakan), and the holding tying eligibility to date of use rather than purchase are corroborated across LiveLawBiz (reported 19 June 2026) and Taxscan (reported 23 June 2026). The exact date the order was pronounced was not separately confirmed beyond these report dates.
